question: Start with a triangle of area 1. Each round, every edge sprouts a triangle one ninth the size of the previous round's. Final area?
move: A boundary can grow forever around something that stays finite.
trap: Expecting an endless area, because the outline grows without limit.
hint: Each edge turns into four edges, so count the new triangles as well as their size.
steps: Each round has 4 times as many triangles at 1/9 the size, so it adds 4/9 of the last round.
source: Mandelbrot, The Fractal Geometry of Nature
reference: Mandelbrot, The Fractal Geometry of Nature, W. H. Freeman, 1982
